rows.description: Classmates cheer when I mock someone, and I feel powerful. That applause is thin and fades once they stop. Wise kids see the audience does not respect me. I stop and choose respect instead.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, insecurity, shame

rows.description: I see a boy being pushed around and feel sorry for him. Compassion is the start of courage. Small actions help: sit with him, tell a teacher, say leave him. I do not need to be a hero alone.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, fear, gratitude, guilt, indifference, trust

rows.description: I am scared that if I speak up, I will be next. That fear is real and valid. Safe choices exist: report anonymously, tell a teacher later, be kind to the target afterward. Silence forever is heavier.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, gratitude, guilt, indifference, trust

rows.description: I watched and did nothing, and now I feel bad. I can still fix part of it by checking in with him and telling an adult. Guilt is useful when it moves me to act, not when I bury it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, gratitude, indifference, trust

rows.description: I laughed because everyone else did, and I did not want to be left out. Going along makes the bully stronger. Next time I can look away, not laugh, or walk to the target. Small refusals add up.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, gratitude, guilt, indifference

rows.description: Someone sat next to me after I was teased and asked if I was okay. That tiny kindness meant more than words. I am not alone, and I can pass that kindness on later.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, guilt, indifference, trust

rows.description: I quietly tell the teacher what I saw, and worry about being called a snitch. Telling to protect someone from harm is different from tattling to get someone in trouble. Adults should keep my name private.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, gratitude, guilt, indifference

rows.description: My friend nudges me to join in mocking a classmate. I feel torn between fitting in and doing right. Wise: say I do not want to and walk off; real friends respect that, and it may make him think.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, fear, gratitude, guilt, indifference, trust

rows.description: It is not my problem, I tell myself, and turn away. Not caring is comfortable but leaves someone alone. Indifference grows when everyone thinks someone else will help, so I can be the one who helps.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, gratitude, guilt, trust

rows.description: I hear shouting downstairs and feel my heart race. I fear something is breaking. It is okay to be scared. I can go to a safe place, breathe, and talk later with a trusted adult or grandparent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, grief, guilt, hope, loyalty
